learning_objectives: Choose the correct gender and number for regular four-ending adjectives.
Use regular two-ending adjectives in singular and plural with either gender.
Keep noun–adjective agreement both after nouns and after essere.

skills.description_en: Recognise and form masculine and feminine singular endings (-o, -a) for regular four-ending adjectives.
Recognise and form masculine and feminine plural endings (-i, -e) for regular four-ending adjectives.
Use the same -e adjective form with masculine and feminine singular nouns.
Use -i with masculine and feminine plurals of regular two-ending adjectives.
Match adjectives to nouns both after the noun and after essere.
Correct, transform, and independently produce adjective–noun agreement.

lesson.short_explanation_en: In Italian, a describing adjective usually changes to agree with the noun it describes in gender (masculine/feminine) and number (singular/plural). Regular adjectives ending in -o have four forms: nuovo, nuova, nuovi, nuove. Regular adjectives ending in -e have two: grande in the singular and grandi in the plural, for both genders. Agreement also applies after essere: la casa è nuova; le case sono nuove.

rule_blocks.explanation_en: Start from the masculine singular dictionary form ending in -o. Use -a for feminine singular, -i for masculine plural and -e for feminine plural.
usage_notes_en: First find the noun’s gender and number.
Change the adjective ending to match that noun.
Examples in this lesson use regular four-ending adjectives; some other adjectives have spelling changes.
common_errors_en: Not *la penna nuovo*: use la penna nuova.
Not *i libri nuove*: use i libri nuovi.

rule_blocks.explanation_en: Adjectives such as grande and felice use the same -e form with singular masculine and singular feminine nouns. For either gender in the plural, use -i.
rule_blocks.pattern: il bambino felice / la bambina felice → i bambini felici / le bambine felici
usage_notes_en: No separate masculine and feminine endings for regular -e adjectives.
common_errors_en: Not *la bambina felica*: use la bambina felice.
Not *le bambine felice*: use le bambine felici.

rule_blocks.heading_en: Agreement next to a noun or after essere
rule_blocks.explanation_en: An adjective agrees with its noun in a noun phrase (uno zaino piccolo) and also when linked by essere (lo zaino è piccolo). The place of the adjective does not remove agreement.
rule_blocks.pattern: una borsa piccola; la borsa è piccola
usage_notes_en: For the vocabulary in this lesson, adjective-after-noun is a useful neutral pattern.
More subtle changes in meaning caused by adjective position belong to a later lesson.
common_errors_en: Not *due borse piccolo*: use due borse piccole.

contexts.setting_en: Anna and Marco look at the rooms in an apartment.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Sì, ma le camere sono grandi.
lines.translation_en: Yes, but the bedrooms are large.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Le finestre sono grandi. Il balcone è piccolo.
lines.translation_en: The windows are large. The balcony is small.

focus_items.explanation_en: Cucina is a feminine singular noun, so piccolo becomes piccola.
Grande takes -i in the plural, regardless of gender.

contexts.setting_en: Anna messages Marco after shopping for food.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.target: Oggi le mele sono buone. I pomodori sono rossi.
lines.translation_en: Today the apples are good. The tomatoes are red.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.target: Le banane sono grandi e il pane è buono.
lines.translation_en: The bananas are large, and the bread is good.

focus_items.explanation_en: Mele is feminine plural: buono becomes buone.
Pomodori is masculine plural, so rosso changes to rossi.
Banane is feminine plural: grande becomes grandi.

examples.note_en: Felice has the same singular form for both genders.
Felice does not take a separate feminine singular ending.
Felice becomes felici in the plural.
The plural form felici works for feminine nouns too.
The adjective piccolo follows the noun and agrees with masculine singular zaino.
Piccole follows feminine plural borse; the ending changes to -e.
